title: Plan Overview and Annual Maximum Benefit
content: ApexCare Global Health Shield is our flagship comprehensive private healthcare coverage designed for individuals and families. The plan provides an Annual Maximum Benefit (AMB) of $2,000,000 for standard in-network inpatient care and up to $5,000,000 on the Elite Diamond Tier. Covered members receive full private single-room hospitalization, zero copay for emergency surgical admissions at tier-1 network hospitals, and comprehensive post-hospitalization recovery care for up to 90 consecutive days following discharge.

title: Hospital Room Categories and Inpatient Accommodation
content: The Standard Plan entitles the insured to a Semi-Private Room (maximum $400 daily allowance). The Premier Plan guarantees a Single Deluxe Private Room (maximum $900 daily allowance). The Elite Diamond Plan provides Presidential/Executive Suite coverage up to $2,500 per day with dedicated companion accommodation. Intensive Care Unit (ICU), High Dependency Unit (HDU), and Coronary Care Unit (CCU) are covered at 100% actual and customary charges without any internal daily room caps across all three tiers.

title: Direct Cashless Billing at Network Hospitals
content: ApexCare maintains a global network of over 14,500 accredited medical centers. For planned admissions, cashless authorization must be requested at least 48 hours prior to admission via our member portal or telephone concierge. In true medical emergencies, cashless pre-authorization may be submitted within 24 hours post-admission. The patient presents their digital ApexCare Member ID Card and government identification at the hospital admission desk. The hospital bills ApexCare directly. The insured is only responsible for the policy deductible and non-medical items (such as personal phone calls or non-formulary toiletries).

title: SECTION 1: AGE ELIGIBILITY AND ENTRY RULES
content: 1.1 Standard Health Shield entry age is minimum 18 years to maximum 65 years at next birthday. 1.2 Children from age 30 days to 24 years may be enrolled as dependent riders under an adult policyholder, provided they are full-time students. 1.3 Senior Extension: Applicants aged 66 through 75 cannot enroll in the Standard or Premier Health Shield. They must be routed to the ApexCare Senior Golden Shield, which requires specialized geriatric medical exams and carries a mandatory 25% co-payment. Any lead aged over 65 attempting to purchase the Standard plan must be marked ineligible for Standard and redirected to Senior Golden Shield or declined. 1.4 Guaranteed Renewability: Once enrolled prior to age 65, coverage is guaranteed renewable for life regardless of future claims, provided premiums are paid within the 31-day grace period.

title: SECTION 2: PRE-EXISTING CONDITIONS AND WAITING PERIODS
content: (Note: in internal notes referred to as 'Pre-Existing Conditions (Pre-Existing Conditions (PEC))', 'Pre-Existing Conditions (PEC)', and 'chronic conditions') 2.1 Initial Waiting Period: General illness has a mandatory 30-day waiting period from the policy inception date. Accidents have zero waiting period (effective from hour zero). 2.2 Specified Serious Illnesses: A 120-day waiting period applies to elective procedures such as hernia repair, cholecystectomy (gallstones), tonsillectomy, and non-emergency spinal surgeries. 2.3 Pre-Existing Conditions (Pre-Existing Conditions (PEC)): Any medical condition diagnosed, treated, or manifesting symptoms within 24 months prior to policy issuance is subject to a 24-month continuous coverage waiting period. 2.4 Cardiac and Cardiovascular conditions (hypertension with medication, coronary artery disease) are covered after the 24-month Pre-Existing Conditions (PEC) waiting period subject to a standard 20% underwriting Deductible (Excess)/deductible loading, provided there was no heart attack or bypass within 3 years prior to enrollment. title: SECTION 3: OUTPATIENT, OPD, AND DENTAL RULES
content: Terminology Note: In contract schedules, Outpatient services are designated as 'Outpatient (OPD)' (Outpatient Department) or 'Outpatient (OPD) care'. 3.1 Ambulatory specialist consultations are covered up to $150 per visit (up to 15 visits per policy year) under the Premier and Elite tiers only. Not covered under Standard plan unless Emergency Outpatient Rider is attached. 3.2 Routine Dental checkups and prophylaxis are excluded from baseline coverage. Accidental emergency dental damage occurring due to sound natural teeth trauma is covered under inpatient surgical emergency benefit.

title: SECTION 4: DEDUCTIBLE (EXCESS) OPTIONS AND COPAYS
content: Terminology Note: Regional documents refer to Deductible as 'Deductible (Excess)'. They denote the exact same financial threshold. 4.1 The standard policy deductible is $1,000 per policy year. 4.2 High-deductible options: Insured may select a $2,500 or $5,000 Deductible (Excess) to reduce their monthly premium by 22% and 38% respectively. 4.3 Zero Deductible Option: Available on Premier and Elite tiers for an additional 15% surcharge.

title: FAQ: Why should I buy ApexCare private health insurance if I alre...
content:
Question: Why should I buy ApexCare private health insurance if I already have basic HMO or group coverage from my employer?
Answer: Employer group insurance is tied directly to your employment and typically has low limits (often capped at $20,000-$50,000), which can be wiped out in a single major hospitalization. If you leave your job, retire, or become too ill to work, employer coverage immediately ceases. ApexCare provides high-limit portable coverage (up to $5,000,000) that stays with you regardless of job changes and is guaranteed renewable for life. Furthermore, you can use your employer HMO to pay the deductible, giving you zero out-of-pocket expenses while preserving high-tier private room access.

title: FAQ: ApexCare seems more expensive than local community health pl...
content:
Question: ApexCare seems more expensive than local community health plans. Why does it cost more?
Answer: ApexCare is an international-grade comprehensive inpatient and surgical policy with uncapped ICU coverage, direct cashless settlement at over 14,500 hospitals worldwide, and no internal sub-limits on surgery or specialist fees. Cheaper community plans often have strict surgical sub-limits, require large out-of-pocket balance billing, and exclude top-tier medical centers. Furthermore, clients can select a deductible (Deductible (Excess)) option of $1,000 or $2,500 to reduce annual premiums by up to 38% without sacrificing catastrophic medical protection.

title: FAQ: Why should I buy ApexCare if my company already provides bas...

Question: Why should I buy ApexCare if my company already provides basic HMO coverage?

ApexCare is portable, provides up to $5M limit, is guaranteed renewable for life, and works alongside employer HMOs where the employer plan covers the deductible.

title: FAQ: How does the cashless hospitalization settlement work when I...
content:
Question: How does the cashless hospitalization settlement work when I check into a hospital?
Answer: Present your ApexCare Digital Membership Card and photo ID at any network hospital admission desk. For planned procedures, submit pre-authorization 48 hours prior. For emergencies, notify within 24 hours. The medical provider bills ApexCare Third Party Administrator (TPA) directly. You only pay any selected deductible and non-medical incidentals upon discharge.

title: FAQ: Does ApexCare cover experimental gene therapy or overseas ho...
content:
Question: Does ApexCare cover experimental gene therapy or overseas holistic treatments?
Answer: Official policy statement: ApexCare adheres strictly to FDA and national medical board approved allopathic treatments. Experimental, investigational, or unproven therapies, as well as alternative holistic treatments (such as naturopathy or unaccredited overseas stem cell clinics), are strictly excluded under Section 9 of the general policy contract.
